title: Looking for Beta testers ($)
author: orellanaed
selftext:
Hi ai game devs, for the past year or so I have been working on a tool to develop PC games with AI with a real game engine. I am now looking for beta testers.

Requirements: Windows 10+, and conditional to a short 30min interview to collect feedback after trying it out

I am a solo founder so the most I can do is a **$25 gift card** for your time. If interested please comment or send me a DM. Thanks!

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: Tried to send you a dm but it won't let me. Send me a DM or email me at support@flockbay.com

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body: Interested. Seems like you're patching the model through Godot. I tried that late last year to mixed results. Been using Unity lately.

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: Yeah, basically, but with a lot of runtime/tooling around it. I get the mixed results though. Raw LLM + engine access is not enough. The hard part is making the workflow reliable enough that it produces real projects instead of broken demos or AI slop

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body: Lots of screenshots from the right angles and mandatory smoke testing seems to have helped. Tbh my orchestrator has grown so large, I don't fully know all the tools it and it's sub-agent use. Usually just a session post-mortem "update the skill and memory from lessons learned in this session and build the tools that either automate the work you shouldn't have had to do or ensure accuracy of the work you did do". Probably close to 100 sessions at this point. Then a meta session to shave it back down/split out knowledge and tools to sub-agents every 10-20 sessions. Seems to have worked well though. Environment generation has been an absolute bitch though.

comments.author: MadJagStudios
comments.body: Is it an AI wrapper that integrates with godot? Not that it’s a bad thing, just curious before I invest any time into looking into it as a legit option

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: No, not just a generic AI wrapper around Godot. I run a Godot-focused model/context layer with a custom trained LLM, but the bigger difference is the tool/runtime stack around it. The goal is a real AI game-builder workflow, not just ChatGPT attached to Godot

replies.author: MadJagStudios
replies.body: I’ve got a game idea I want to start, I’d be down to try it out

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body:
That’s exactly the kind of background I’d be curious to get feedback from.

Godot has been a good fit because it is lightweight, open source and exports cleanly to desktop. If you're interested in participating in the beta I’d be most interested in where the workflow breaks down compared to Unity/Three.js

Sending you a DM
